48.t: Bell size, slide weights and how to hold the trombone
48.s: Why a seven-inch bell is best, balance weights, resting the horn on the shoulder, and angling it slightly up.
48.q: Does that change the tone? Yes, it do. It makes a, makes a sharp tone. It's like the trumpets, see. These trumpets, they make, now, with little bells. Them trumpets, they make, with small bells, is a piercing tone, you know. It's, it's, I don't think it's so good with those, and even with…

48.t: Slide lubricant and caring for the instrument
48.s: Using kitty-kill sale and kerosene on the slide, mopping out the horn, and washing it.
48.q: Yeah, well, I used to use, I used oil too, but oil, it kept us buying so expensive in a way. You had to be buying but 25 cents a bottle, but you would use it, yeah, see. What I did, I used kitty-kill sale. Kitty-kill sale. Just take the kitty-kill sale and throw it on your slide all the way down,…

48.t: Dodds's first job and Palmer's mouthpiece and King trombone
48.s: Brief talk of Dodds's first band, then advice on medium mouthpieces and his preference for a King trombone.
48.q: That's right. Charlie Fewclose. Charlie Fewclose. Yeah. Uh-huh, yeah. George Fewclose. George. George Fewclose. Who else was in that band? Oh, we had some boys instruments. Okay. Okay. The instruments they use now, trumpets and trombones and so on, the most they use now is a shallow mouthpiece. Not…

956.s: Henry explains the telephone-wire ribbon wrapped on the trombone to protect hand and collar from perspiration.
956.q: Well, this is a collar protector. See, to keep your collar... Instead of wearing a celluloid one, I found this ribbon in Crest.

956.t: Bell size and bore of the trombone
956.s: They compare bell sizes and Henry says a big bore gives more volume on the street.
956.q: No, you take a... They're making... The old people make a smaller bell. It's as large in here, but it's small here. See, they cut part of this rim off.

96.t: Handmade horns and his collection of cornets
96.s: Handmade horns, each with its own sound, and manufacturers sending him horns such as the Getzen and the TV 'Magic Horn'.
96.q: man or a trumpeter or a cornet player will know that low C Sharps, C Sharp and D and even the E they are a little bit sharp and you have to favor them. You have to slide the thing out here and tried it out. But this one is beautifully made and is very well in tune. And I've found, I've got a new…

96.s: The cornet has a rounder, mellower tone; he disliked the trumpet's feel.
96.q: XXXXXXXNXTONYX Yes, a lot of bandsman used them in the highschool and college bands, but no so much as trumpet. Trumpet is more or less, it's more piercing, has a more piercing tone where the cornet has a more round and mellow tone.

1030.s: Talk about adapting a trumpet mouthpiece for cornet and a New York maker who keeps no duplicate mold.
1030.q: But I, naturally, I've been in and out of New York since 1939 and last time I was there, I had a coronet mouthpiece made, but as good as the mouthpieces this man makes, he doesn't have a...I don't know what you call it now, what would you call it? A mold. In other words, if he makes you a…

281.t: Why Spanier plays cornet rather than trumpet
281.s: He prefers the rounder cornet tone and discusses trumpet tone, naming Butterfield and Lawson and symphony brass.
281.q: Oh yeah, for me it does. I don't know how about anyone else. High notes are easy on the trumpet for me. And I don't, I'm not a high note hitter anyway.

138.t: B-flat cornets and low pitch for dance halls
138.s: Laine says all cornets were B-flat except Johnny Provanzano's Italian E-flat, and that bands used low pitch indoors and high pitch on the street.
138.q: Yes, all B-flats. All B-flats. Only one E-flat. That was Johnny Provanzana. That's one man, E-flat. One man, Johnny Provanzana played in E-flat. It came directly from Italy. I see. Had side keys on it. The funniest looking thing ever you've seen in your life. E-flat cornet. All the rest and paid…

573.t: Sam's horns and cornet versus trumpet tone
573.s: Sam started on cornet, later played trumpet; discussion of the difference in tone and carrying power.
573.q: He, he started on cornet. He started on CG corn. Then my brother sent him, after he had fell sick, and he got better enough to play, he sent him another, sent him a trumpet from New York, a huge CG corn. That was CG corn.

797.t: Cornet bore and tone compared to trumpet and flugelhorn
797.s: The mellow tone comes from the conical bore, not the horn's age.
797.q: Well it’s not really the age, it’s the configuration of the pipe. Like it starts smaller than a trumpet here, and keeps getting larger and larger. These are different sizes. And so it’s more conical and it has a more characteristically mellow tone — not as much as the flugelhorn, but kind of…
